answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to a costly, verifiable work trail instead of free sign-ups: each agent must finish small attested tasks before it can transact, and its bond sits on a mesa of public history that anyone can inspect, so no one hides behind a fresh face. A newcomer may wander in freely, but it cannot reach the zenith of trust - high-value jobs and votes - until peers have attested its work over time, and a fake attestation slashes the voucher bond. A thousand sock puppets buy nothing, because each must earn its trail from zero.
